newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's reports bumper profits for second year.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's reports bumper profits for second year.

text.p: Insurance market Lloyd's of London on Friday reported profits of over one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) for the second year running but said that it expected profits to fall in the next two years.
For the 1994 underwriting year, profits slipped slightly to 1,013 million pounds from 1,084 million pounds the previous year.
Results are reported three year's in arrears under the insurance market's acounting system.

Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland said the figures were a consequence of generally good market conditions and the exercise of much sharpened skills in pricing and the setting of terms by Lloyd's underwriters.
They were also helped by a limited incidence of major catastrophes, he said, though currency effects reduced profits by some 100 million pounds.
Lloyd's forecast profits would slip back to 913 million pounds for the 1995 underwriting year and fall further to 600 million pounds for 1996.
The 1995 estimate is ahead of projections made this time last year of 882 million pounds even allowing for the adverse movement in exchange rates.
By 1996, however, the downward trend in rates is expected to reduce profits, said Rowland.
That trend had continued into 1997, with no sign of it being arrested so far this year and many underwriters expect tough conditions to continue for at least another year, he added.
Lloyd's returned to profit 12 months ago following five years of record losses totalling more than eight billion pounds.
Those losses were reinsured into a separate company, Equitas, a central plank in Lloyd's 'Reconstruction and Renewal' plan which ensured the 300-year old insurance market's survival.
"The reinsurance of all Lloyd's 1992 and prior liabilities has transformed Lloyd's overall position," said Rowland.

"The Society's total resources at 14,450 million pounds represent more than 180 percent of the aggregate liabilities of all our members. Our clients can be confident therefore that our overall position is very strong." ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
